title: Strict scalar pullback cone maps and their derived naturality
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $W=X,Y$, $F=E,L$, $m\ge1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the quotient maps $\iota_m:\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m\to\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ and $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For any cochain complex $P$ of $R_Y$-modules put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$; tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$-complex $M$ put
$$D^F_m(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD^F_m(M)\to\prod_mD^F_m(M))[-1],$$
using module inverse image $g_{F,m}^*=g^{-1}(-)\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{F,Y,m}}B_{F,X,m}$, coefficient structure maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction of scalars and quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. There is a natural strict tower map $d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to D^L_m(Q)$ uniquely specified on local tensor generators by
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto(g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)).$$
These formulas are balanced, commute with the cochain differentials and every quotient transition, and are natural in all chain maps $P\to P'$. Since $S_X$ is a finite free $R_X$-module [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], the canonical tensor/product maps are isomorphisms, independent of a choice of finite free basis of $S_X$ over $R_X$, and identify $A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with the Roos cone of $D^E_\bullet(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$. The induced chain map $\delta_P$ to $A_L(Q)$ sends both cone coordinates by $\prod_m d_m$. On flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex], these chain maps descend to a natural transformation
$$C_X Lg_E^*\longrightarrow Lg_L^* C_Y,\qquad C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W,$$
with representative $[\delta_P]$ under the canonical comparison isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. In particular the represented morphism is independent of the K-flat resolution and natural for arbitrary derived morphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $E\subset L\subset F$ the level maps and cone maps compose to those for $E\subset F$ after the canonical tensor associators; for $L=E$ they are identities under the tensor unit identifications.

proof.text: Write $a_W:R_W\to S_W$, $j_{W,m}:B_{E,W,m}\to B_{L,W,m}$ and $c_{F,m}:g^{-1}B_{F,Y,m}\to B_{F,X,m}$ for the coefficient maps. The inverse-limit map $a_W$ satisfies $\pi^L_ma_W=j_{W,m}\pi^E_m$: its components are precisely the compatible maps $\iota_m\pi^E_m$. Moreover $c_{L,m}g^{-1}(j_{Y,m})=j_{X,m}c_{E,m}$. Indeed the adjoints of both sides send a constant section $\bar a$ to the constant section $\iota_m(\bar a)$ on each base change; the sheafification universal property and the inverse-image adjunction in the cited definition give equality. The same argument gives compatibility with quotient transitions. Use throughout the explicit associator $Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}\cong P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$, $((p\otimes s)\otimes z)\mapsto p\otimes\pi^L_m(s)z$, whose inverse is $p\otimes z\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes z$. Thus the symbol $p$ in the target generator formula means $p\otimes1$ in $Q$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensors and associativity; coefficient square checked from the cited inverse-image definition

proof.text: Define the additive generator map $f_m:P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y,m}\to P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}$ by $p\otimes\bar a\mapsto p\otimes j_{Y,m}(\bar a)$. It is balanced since $j_{Y,m}(\pi^E_m(r)\bar a)=\rho_m(r)j_{Y,m}(\bar a)$. Apply $g^{-1}$ to $f_m$, and send $((g^{-1}z)\otimes b)\otimes s$ to $(g^{-1}f_m(z))\otimes j_{X,m}(b)\pi^L_m(s)$. For $h\in g^{-1}B_{E,Y,m}$, moving $h$ from $z$ to $b$ gives the same value by $c_{L,m}g^{-1}j_{Y,m}=j_{X,m}c_{E,m}$. For $r\in R_X$, moving $r$ from the first outer tensor factor to $s$ gives the same value because $j_{X,m}(\pi^E_m(r))=\pi^L_m(a_X(r))$. Additivity in every variable and $S_X$-linearity are immediate from multiplication. These identities persist under restrictions, so the sheaf tensor universal property produces a unique map $d_m$ with the required formula. The argument is about local tensor generators and their sheafification, and does not assert that every section globally is a pure tensor.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: bilinear maps and tensor relations

proof.text: Only the $p$ coordinate has a cochain differential. Applying $d_m$ before or after the differential therefore gives the same generator with $p$ replaced by $d_Pp$. If $u:P\to P'$ is a chain map, the two paths in its naturality square both give $(g^{-1}(u(p)\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)$. Finally, reducing the level-$m+1$ formula to level $m$ replaces $\bar a,b,s$ by their quotient images. The identities $\operatorname{red}_L\iota_{m+1}=\iota_m\operatorname{red}_E$ and $\operatorname{red}_L\pi^L_{m+1}=\pi^L_m$, together with the coefficient square of Step 1, show that its value equals the level-$m$ formula. Hence $d_\bullet$ is a strict tower map, natural in chain maps, not merely a collection of derived level maps.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; strict transition calculation using the quotient maps in def-weil-integral-scalar-extension

proof.text: For any family of $R_X$-module sheaves $V_m$, let $\kappa:(\prod_mV_m)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to\prod_m(V_m\otimes_{R_X}S_X)$ have $m$th projection $\operatorname{pr}_m\otimes1$. The cited completed-scalar comparison gives a finite free basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $S_X$. In its coordinates the inverse of $\kappa$ sends $(\sum_jv_{mj}\otimes e_j)_m$ to $\sum_j(v_{mj})_m\otimes e_j$. These are inverse sheaf maps: both composite identities hold on every coordinate, using the finite sum over $j$. This is a degreewise argument for arbitrary unbounded complexes. The forward map was defined entirely by projections, so its inverse and the isomorphism are independent of the basis. Naturality follows by composing with each projection. The same finite-sum formulas identify tensor of a binary biproduct with the biproduct of the tensors, and tensor of a shifted complex with the shift of the tensor.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; explicit finite-basis calculation, using the finite-free assertion of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison

proof.text: Put $V=\prod_mD^E_m(P)$ and $V'=\prod_mD^L_m(Q)$. Under $\kappa$, the image of the transition endomorphism is the transition endomorphism of the tensor tower: both have $m$th projection $(t_m\otimes1)\operatorname{pr}_{m+1}$. Thus the tensor/product and binary-sum identifications of Step 4 identify $A_E(P)\otimes S_X$ with the shifted cone of $1-s$ on that tensor tower. Put $\mu=\prod_md_m$. Step 3 says $\mu(1-s)=(1-s')\mu$. In the coordinates of the cited strict Roos model the differential is $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$. The map $(y,x)\mapsto(\mu y,\mu x)$ commutes with it, since its first coordinate is $-d\mu y-(1-s')\mu x$ and its second is $d\mu x$. This is the specified $\delta_P$. Chain naturality follows from the generator naturality of Step 3 and the projection naturality of $\kappa$. In particular no choice of a third map of a distinguished triangle enters.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; explicit signed diagonal cone calculation

proof.text: Represent $K\in D(R_Y)$ by a complex $K_0$ of $R_Y$-modules. Apply the cited resolution theorem to $K_0$ to choose a degreewise-surjective quasi-isomorphism $P\to K_0$ with $P$ flat-term K-flat; its localization identifies $[P]$ with $K$. Apply K-flat change of rings to $R_Y\to S_Y$: $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ is flat-term K-flat over $S_Y$, and derived change of rings identifies $[Q]$ with $C_YK$. The integral-operation comparison identifies $[A_E(P)]$ with $Lg_E^*K$ and $[A_L(Q)]$ with $Lg_L^*(C_YK)$, with natural comparison isomorphisms on these representatives. Here $g:X\to Y$ is any scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible on $X,Y$; the cited operation theorem and K-flat theorem apply to these ringed sites for unbounded complexes. These are the completed pullback functors of the stated integral-operation definition.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; Tag 06YT and construction preceding 06YU; completed-pullback context Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.9(4)

proof.text: The source of $\delta_P$ also has the required derived interpretation even though $A_E(P)$ need not be K-flat. Indeed tensoring with $S_X\cong R_X^{\oplus d}$ is exact: on underlying $R_X$-module sheaves it is the finite direct sum of $d$ copies, and kernels and cokernels of $S_X$-module maps have their underlying module kernels and cokernels. The exact-functor factorization therefore computes its derived functor on every complex by termwise tensor. This factorization is canonically the derived change-of-rings functor $C_X$: on a K-flat resolution both are the same tensor complex by the change-of-rings comparison, and exactness makes the tensor of the resolution a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $[A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X]$ is canonically $C_XLg_E^*K$. This uses finite freeness of the completed coefficient sheaf, not flatness of the ramified finite quotient maps $\iota_m$.

source.place: Tag 06YT and construction preceding 06YU, specialized to an exact finite-free tensor functor; exact localization factorization recorded in lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization

proof.text: The constructions on representatives respect cochain homotopy. If $u-v=dh+hd$, applying reduction and finite pullback to $h$ gives level homotopies $h_m$ commuting with every quotient transition; tensor with $S_X$ also preserves this homotopy identity by additivity. The strict Roos homotopy theorem then supplies the cone homotopy $(y,x)\mapsto(-\prod_mh_m(y),\prod_mh_m(x))$. Thus both sides of the naturality square of Step 5 give functors on the homotopy category of flat-term K-flat representatives, and $[\delta_P]$ is a natural transformation there. For a quasi-isomorphism $u:P\to P'$, derived change of rings makes $u\otimes S_Y$ a quasi-isomorphism between flat-term K-flat complexes; the integral-operation invariance theorem makes both corresponding $A_E$ and $A_L$ maps quasi-isomorphisms. Exactness of tensor with $S_X$ from Step 7 makes the remaining outer tensor map a quasi-isomorphism. Both functors therefore invert the representative quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and explicit strict Roos homotopy theorem; quasi-isomorphism invariance from sites-cohomology Tags 06YT and 0G7E

proof.text: Apply the resolving-class localization equivalence of the cited site-derived-tensor descent theorem to the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R_Y)$, taking a skeleton small relative to the module universe as in the pro-etale inverse-image convention. Its statement gives $W^{-1}\mathcal P_{R_Y}\simeq D(R_Y)$ for precisely the flat-term K-flat homotopy representatives used in Step 8. Apply the localization universal property for natural transformations to the two functors of Step 8 and $[\delta_P]$, then transport across this equivalence. Conjugating by the canonical comparisons of Steps 6 and 7 gives $C_XLg_E^*\Rightarrow Lg_L^*C_Y$ with the asserted representative. This proves naturality on all derived morphisms. Explicitly, naturality for a representative quasi-isomorphism $w$ gives $G(w)[\delta_P]=[\delta_{P'}]F(w)$; invertibility yields naturality for $[w]^{-1}$ as well, and localization extends this through composites. The universal property's uniqueness shows that replacing $P$ by any other flat-term K-flat resolution gives the same component under the canonical resolution comparisons, including comparisons of a third resolution. No assertion that all derived morphisms lift to individual chain maps is used.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; fully faithful precomposition for natural transformations as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property; resolving-class equivalence from sites-cohomology Tags 06YS and 0G7D

proof.text: For a triple $E\subset L\subset F$, write $j_{LF}:S_{L,X}\to S_{F,X}$ for the completed coefficient map. The same-index quotient maps satisfy $\iota_{LF,m}\iota_{EL,m}=\iota_{EF,m}$, since they all send the class of an integral element to its class in the final quotient. On a generator $(((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s)\otimes t$, the successive level maps give first coordinate $g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_{EF,m}(\bar a))$ and final multiplier $\iota_{EF,m}(b)\pi^F_m(j_{LF}(s))\pi^F_m(t)$. The direct level map after associating the scalar tensors gives the same multiplier $\iota_{EF,m}(b)\pi^F_m(j_{LF}(s)t)$. The target associator on $P\otimes S_L\otimes S_F$ is multiplication on the scalar factors, as in Step 1. Equality on generators and sheafification therefore prove composition of $d_m$. The product comparisons respect these associators: their $m$th projections are all the tensor of $\operatorname{pr}_m$ followed by the same scalar multiplication. Hence the two composite cone maps agree on each of their two coordinates. For $L=E$, $\iota_m$ is the quotient identity and the formula becomes multiplication by $\pi^E_m(s)$, exactly the tensor unitor. The product and cone comparisons then also become their unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: associativity and units; explicit same-index quotient and cone-coordinate calculation

proof.text: For the triple extension use $P$, $P\otimes S_L$ and $P\otimes S_F$, related by the tensor associators, as resolving representatives. They are flat-term K-flat by change of rings. The canonical derived associators on these models are the localized ordinary tensor associators, by the K-flat computation of successive change of rings; equivalently the ordinary map $((p\otimes s)\otimes t)\mapsto p\otimes j_{LF}(s)t$ identifies the two computations and respects every resolution map. Thus the equality of cone maps in Step 10 is the required equality after the canonical derived associators on representatives. Faithfulness of restriction along the resolving-class localization and uniqueness in the localization universal property extend it to all derived objects. The same reasoning with the tensor unitor gives the derived identity comparison for $L=E$.
